confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on three web searches. These found crowdsourced cost-of-living aggregates for Chania and Crete (traveltables, livingcost, expatistan, mylifeelsewhere and nomad.watch). They give about USD 10–13 for an inexpensive meal, USD 27–48 for a mid-range meal for two, USD 3–3.7 for a cappuccino and USD 4.9–5.7 for a 0.5L draught beer. Several of these sources are dated 2023 or carry no date. I raised the figures moderately to reflect peak-season tourist-area pricing in July 2026. The cocktail anchor uses the expatistan crowdsourced average of €9, which is based on few data points. A Chania bar guide in the results lists €8–13 for cocktails and €5–9 for wine by the glass, but it gives no date. I converted euros to USD at about 1.10, which I derived from the RBA AUD/USD and AUD/EUR mid-rates of 18 Nov 2026. The four accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge, not from searches. Chania has very few registered hostels, and July is peak season, so the dorm and hostel private room anchors are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Chania with other Greek island and resort towns that have strong summer demand, such as Heraklion, Rethymno and Corfu Town. Food prices there are a little below Athens' tourist centre, while peak-season room rates are higher than in mainland mid-sized cities.
